Overseer front arm v6

Front v5d (4 x 6/4 carbon tubes) passed solid and strength but read 131 Hz vertical / 162 Hz lateral against 190 Hz: the tubes bend almost on their own. v6 ties them into a carbon truss: 12 x 3.0 diagonals, Warren, 3 panels on every face, printed nodes, and a solid shoulder wedge where the vertical shear crosses into the root.

Options, modal what-if on the v5d arm (4 inserts, h 1.5, E)

OptionVertical HzLateral HzGrid gTarget
v6 chosen: diagonals + nodes + solid shoulder wedge198234327meets 190
tri10: diagonals + nodes + 10 mm triangle walls192226318meets 190
v5d as it is (4 tubes, no diagonals)131162242under 190

Rods only, no new PETG: 160 / 175 Hz. The shoulder band (x 5..25) is the soft spot: stiffening it alone gave 260 Hz. Grid g is PETG + carbon on the FE grid, before the topology rerun moves material. The solid wedge costs about 9 g over tri10 for 5.5 Hz more margin (DEFAULT). Every rod is 50 to 71 mm (C), slides in from its root-side end (rodcheck on the setup: 16/16 clear).

v6 run result (27 Oct)

330.4 g PETG (M) + tubes and rods ~22 g (E); solid_check PASS on the run mesh; strength worst 0.37 (cage crash 7), inside the 0.5 target; first modes 182 Hz vertical / 214 Hz lateral on the 4 inserts, 188 / 229 on the plate faces (M, h 1.5): 4 % under 190. With 6/4 tube diagonals the same mesh reads 191 Hz (E). Fourth front miss on the mode target: Spark decides (accept 182 Hz = 1.15 x full-throttle 1P, or a layout change: shorter front arms).
